title: Prevent full process.env being passed to spawned child processes
impact: Reduces risk of accidental secret leakage and limits attack surface when spawning subprocesses.
steps: Identify all spawn/execFile/StdioClientTransport usages (scripts/lib/serviceLauncher.ts, src/mcp/client.ts, github-mcp/server.js diagnostic spawn).

Introduce a helper (e.g. buildChildEnv(baseOverrides: Record<string,string>, allowlist?: string[])) that constructs a minimal env containing only required keys plus a safe, explicit set (MCP_DEFAULT_DIR, GITHUB_MCP_DEFAULT_DIR, MCP_TRANSPORT, GITHUB_MCP_TRANSPORT, NODE_ENV, PATH).

Replace patterns like { ...process.env, ...overrides } with the new helper in serviceLauncher.spawnService, createMcpLauncher, createLangGraphLauncher, McpClient Stdio transport creation, and diagnostic spawn blocks.
Implement a configurable allowlist/denylist via well-documented env variable (e.g. MCP_CHILD_ENV_ALLOWLIST) and unit tests for the helper to ensure only allowed keys are present.
Redact environment variables in logs (do not print full child.env). Add explicit debug logging that lists keys being passed (not values).
Run tests and manual smoke test: start local mcp and langgraph dev flows to ensure processes still run with minimal env.
acceptance_criteria: All spawn/exec invocations use buildChildEnv and no code spreads process.env into child env.
Unit tests exist for buildChildEnv covering default and allowlist modes.
Logs do not print secret values and only show allowed env keys passed to children.
Manual start/dev flows succeed when only allowed env variables are set.

title: Sanitize server tool error responses and centralize server-side logging
impact: Prevents leakage of internal error messages or sensitive data to remote callers while keeping detailed logs for debugging.
steps: Create a server-side error handling utility (e.g. sanitizeToolError(err): {publicMessage, logContext}).

Modify MCP server CallToolRequestSchema handler in github-mcp/server.js to use sanitizeToolError and return standardized error objects such as { code: 'tool_error', message: 'Tool failed to run' } instead of raw error.message.
Log full error details (message, stack, contextual request info) server-side via console.error or a logging utility, ensuring logs are not exposed to the caller.
Add unit tests that mock tool.run throwing errors and verify the returned content contains sanitized message and isError true.
Document the new error contract in github-mcp/README.md.
acceptance_criteria: Tool call failures return a predictable, generic public error message and isError flag.
Detailed error information (stack, internal paths) appears only in server logs and not in tool responses.
Unit tests validate sanitized responses for thrown errors.

title: Refine fetchUrl allowlist resolution and validation
impact: Improves SSRF defense and prevents misconfiguration or permissive allowlists.
steps: Refactor allowlist resolution in github-mcp/tools/fetchUrl.js to a single function that returns an explicit array: effectiveAllowlist = normalizeAllowlist(allowlist || parseAllowlistFromEnv() || config.fetchAllowlist).
Implement normalizeAllowlist that trims entries, rejects empty strings, validates wildcard and domain syntax, and rejects suspicious patterns (e.g. '*' alone).
Cache parsed allowlist on module load and expose a startup warning if final allowlist is empty, listing recommended safe hosts.
Add unit tests for allowlist normalization covering: exact hosts, '*.example.com' wildcards, invalid entries, empty allowlist.
Add a comment and README guidance describing safe allowlist values and examples.
acceptance_criteria: fetchUrl resolves allowlist using normalized, cached entries and never calls parseAllowlistFromEnv() multiple times per request.
Validation tests cover common good/bad patterns and the function rejects invalid entries.
Startup warns clearly when no allowlist is configured.

title: Harden path resolution by resolving real paths and preventing symlink bypass
impact: Prevents directory traversal via symlinks and ensures file operations are confined to the configured repo.
steps: In github-mcp/tools/pathUtils.js, augment resolveRepoPath to call fs.realpathSync on baseDir and the resolved path to obtain canonical paths.
Update ensurePathInside to compare realpath(base) and realpath(target) using path.relative on canonical paths and still reject targets outside base.
If defaultDir is undefined, require callers to pass an explicit absolute path or modify behavior to treat '.' as unsafe and throw; document the chosen behavior.
Add unit tests: symlink pointing outside base, nested symlink, relative path escapes, and expected success cases.
Document changes in github-mcp/README.md and note the stricter behavior.
acceptance_criteria: resolveRepoPath uses fs.realpath to canonicalize paths before comparison.
Unit tests demonstrate symlink attempts outside base are rejected.
No regressions in tools that rely on resolveRepoPath (run test suite).

title: Sanitize and constrain git command inputs and error outputs
impact: Reduces risk of exposing repo internals to callers and limits resource exhaustion from git operations.
steps: Ensure all callers of runGit pass sanitized arguments; where filePath/user input is used, URL- or shell-escape or normalize using path.resolve and ensure it is inside repo via resolveRepoPath.
Add an explicit whitelist for git subcommands if possible (e.g. only allow blame, log, grep, diff, rev-parse) and assert on args shape before execFile.
Sanitize errors: when runGit catches an error, return a generic 'Git command failed' message to callers and log detailed stderr server-side.
Add tighter defaults for timeoutMs and maxBuffer where missing and add a cap configuration (documented in github-mcp/config).
Add tests that pass large output and ensure maxBuffer and timeouts behave as expected.
acceptance_criteria: runGit rejects unexpected subcommands and sanitizes user-provided file paths via resolveRepoPath.
Git errors returned to remote callers are generic; full stderr is only in logs.
Timeouts and buffer limits prevent unbounded resource usage in typical test scenarios.

title: Harden McpClient transport creation and avoid global polyfills
impact: Prevents global namespace pollution and handles malformed MCP_URL gracefully.
steps: Wrap new URL(mcpUrl) construction in try/catch and validate allowed schemes (http/https) and host patterns; surface an actionable error if invalid.

Avoid assigning EventSource to globalThis; instead provide a scoped polyfill injection approach: allow McpClient.getInstance to accept an optional transports/options param or set EventSource on a module-scoped variable consumed by SSEClientTransport.
When creating StdioClientTransport for local server, use buildChildEnv from T001 so only minimal env is passed.
Add unit tests to ensure invalid MCP_URL values are handled and that EventSource is not globally set in default flows.
Document the transport behavior and how to supply a custom EventSource in README.
acceptance_criteria: McpClient.validate MCP_URL and throws a controlled error with guidance for operators if invalid.
No assignments to globalThis.EventSource remain (unless behind an explicit opt-in flag) and SSE transport works when EventSource is injected locally for tests.
StdioClientTransport spawn uses minimal env as per T001.

title: Sanitize GitHub API errors and add basic retry/backoff for rate limits
impact: Reduces sensitive API error leakage and improves resiliency against transient rate limits.
steps: Change github-mcp/tools/githubApi.js:githubFetchJson to map non-OK responses to a sanitized error (e.g. 'GitHub API responded with status X') and include a limited, structured 'code' field when applicable.
Implement a lightweight retry wrapper for idempotent endpoints that retries on 429 or network timeouts with exponential backoff (configurable maxRetries).
Log full API error JSON server-side rather than including it in the thrown Error message returned to callers.
Add unit tests that simulate 429 and non-2xx responses to verify sanitized messages and retry behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Clients receive sanitized error messages; server logs include full API responses.
Retry/backoff triggers on 429 and gives up after configured retries; tests validate behavior.

title: Make diagnostic mode safer and configurable for CI
impact: Prevents spurious CI failures and orphaned processes when diagnostics are run in automated environments.
steps: Make diagnostic timeout configurable via env var (e.g. MCP_DIAGNOSTIC_TIMEOUT_MS) and default to 60s; avoid killing child processes unconditionally — attempt graceful shutdown then escalate.
Track child PID and use a safer kill sequence: SIGTERM → wait → SIGKILL if necessary. Ensure spawn options include detached: false and proper stdio handling in CI.
Add an option to run diagnostics in non-destructive 'dry' mode that only checks initialization path without spawning full server (for CI).
Update server diagnostic tests and README to describe CI-safe usage.
acceptance_criteria: Diagnostic timeout is configurable and documentation updated.
Diagnostic mode uses a graceful shutdown sequence and provides a non-destructive mode for CI.
CI runs of diagnostic tests do not leave orphaned processes in test runs (validated in CI job or local simulation).

title: Centralize and harden configuration validation; avoid mutating process.env in config module
impact: Clarifies failure modes, avoids surprising global side-effects, and improves observability of missing credentials.
steps: Refactor src/config.ts to return a pure config object and remove code that mutates process.env. Introduce an explicit applyEnvToProcess function used by top-level startup scripts (scripts/start-all.ts, scripts/dev-all.ts) if propagation is needed.

Add a validateConfig() function that checks required credentials (AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT/API_KEY) and either throws (strict mode) or returns warnings depending on a new env flag (CONFIG_STRICT=true/false).
Document expected behavior and add startup logs that clearly state when credentials are missing and what degraded functionality will occur.
Add unit tests for validateConfig behavior in strict and non-strict modes.
acceptance_criteria: src/config.ts no longer mutates process.env at module-import time.
Startup scripts explicitly apply env propagation in one place when needed.
validateConfig enforces credential presence in strict mode and tests cover both modes.
README updated describing config strict mode and required env variables.
